title: Disturbing building fabric: asbestos, lead and silica when drilling and coring
activity: Drilling and core drilling walls, ceilings, slabs and risers to mount detectors and run pipework, in buildings built before 1990 where the asbestos register governs the work.

hrcw.clause: Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld), s 291(d)
hrcw.text: Construction work that involves, or is likely to involve, the disturbance of asbestos

hrcw.clause: Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld), s 291(a)
hrcw.text: Construction work that involves a risk of a person falling more than 2m

hrcw.clause: Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld), s 291(k)
hrcw.text: Construction work that is carried out on or near energised electrical installations or services

hrcw.clause: Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld), s 291(f)
hrcw.text: Construction work that is carried out in or near a confined space

hrcw.clause: Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld), s 291(o)
hrcw.text: Construction work that is carried out in an area at a workplace in which there is any movement of powered mobile plant

whenRequired:
Any time you put a bit into a wall, ceiling, slab, riser or switchboard backing in a building built before 1990 — mounting a detector base, coring for pipework, fixing a bracket, opening a penetration. Also in a building of any age where the asbestos register lists ACM near the drill point, or where the area is recorded as inaccessible or not inspected.

You do not need this SWMS to swap a head off an existing base, or to re-terminate in a penetration that already exists and where no fabric is cut. That exclusion is about THIS document only, and it is not a licence to work without one. Testing, maintenance or repair work of a minor nature carried out in connection with a structure is carved out of the meaning of construction work by Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 289(3)(d), so a head swap is often not high risk construction work at all — but the duty to manage the risk of a fall under Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) ss 78 and 79 does not go away, and Safe QLD requires the working-at-heights SWMS for any head swap off a platform or ladder above 2 m. And if you open the base and find AC sheet behind it, you are back in this document and this document stops the job.

CONFINED SPACES — WHAT THIS SWMS DOES NOT AUTHORISE. This SWMS covers drilling in or near a confined space. It does NOT authorise entry to one. If the riser, ceiling space, pit or duct meets the definition of confined space in Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) schedule 19 — an enclosed or partially enclosed space not intended primarily to be occupied, at normal atmospheric pressure, that is or is likely to be a risk from unsafe oxygen level, airborne contaminants, fire or explosion, or engulfment — stop. Entry needs the confined space SWMS, a confined space entry permit under Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 67, atmospheric testing, a standby person outside and rehearsed rescue under Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 74. Safe QLD crews do not carry gas detectors, tripods or retrieval winches on a detector run, so if it is a confined space the answer today is: do not enter, and call the supervisor.

HOW THE RISK RATINGS IN THIS SWMS ARE SET. Every initialRisk and residualRisk below comes off this key, so you can argue with a rating instead of guessing at it. Consequence is rated for the outcome of THAT STEP failing, on the footing that the later steps in this SWMS are still standing between you and the worst case.
LIKELIHOOD — almost certain (happens most times this task runs) / likely (happens often) / possible (has happened to us or to the trade) / unlikely (would need something to go wrong first) / rare (would need several things to go wrong at once).
CONSEQUENCE — catastrophic (death, or an irreversible disease such as mesothelioma or silicosis) / major (permanent injury, hospital admission, a notifiable incident) / moderate (medical treatment or lost time) / minor (first aid only) / insignificant (no injury).
THE GRID, likelihood down and consequence across (catastrophic, major, moderate, minor, insignificant):
  almost certain — extreme, extreme, high, high, medium
  likely         — extreme, extreme, high, medium, medium
  possible       — extreme, high, medium, medium, low
  unlikely       — high, medium, medium, low, low
  rare           — medium, medium, low, low, low
Initial risk is rated with no controls in place. Residual risk is rated with every control in the step actually working — and it is never rated low where the only things holding it up are paperwork and a respirator. If the controls in a step are not all in place on the day, the residual reverts to the initial rating and you stop.
permits: Site permit to work or drilling permit from the building manager or facilities manager

Fire system impairment permit, with the zone or loop isolated at the FIP and the ASE placed on test with the monitoring provider. The permit carries the agreed time limit for the impairment, the named fire watch, and the HVAC shutdown arranged with the site's mechanical services contractor

Electrical isolation permit with lock-out tag-out at the distribution board, where a circuit in the drill zone must be de-energised. The isolation is performed and proven dead by the site's licensed electrician; you fit your own personal danger lock and keep the only key

Penetration approval from the structural engineer of record for any core through a suspended slab, beam or load-bearing wall, with the tendon and reinforcement mark-up and any no-core zones marked on it
Asbestos removal control plan and a licensed asbestos removalist, where a penetration must be made in ACM — class A for friable at any quantity, class B for more than 10m² of non-friable
Working at heights permit where the site requires one for EWP or platform work
Confined space entry permit — NOT issued under this SWMS. If the riser, ceiling space or pit is a confined space, stop and use the confined space SWMS and its permit
Infection control permit / interim life safety measures approval in a hospital, day surgery or aged-care facility, obtained before the day
Hot work permit is not required for drilling or diamond coring — do not raise one out of habit, and do raise one if the scope changes to cutting, grinding or welding
ppe: P2 half-face respirator, fit-tested, to AS/NZS 1716:2012 and selected and worn per AS/NZS 1715:2009 — clean-shaven at the seal. These are the exact editions Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 529B(3) names, so this is not a matter of preference
Wide-vision goggles or sealed safety glasses to AS/NZS 1337.1 for overhead drilling

Hearing protection selected per AS/NZS 1269.3 from the tool's declared noise data — typically class 4 for rotary hammers, class 5 for the larger core rigs — to AS/NZS 1270. Do not over-protect: you have to hear the evacuation alarm, the spotter on the ground controls, and anyone walking into an area where detection is isolated
Type 5 Category III disposable coveralls, no external pockets, cuffs taped, where any ACM is present or assumed

Cut-resistant gloves. Note deliberately: anti-vibration gloves are NOT worn as a control for hand-arm vibration on this work. They attenuate frequencies above the range that causes hand-arm vibration syndrome and can increase grip force, and so transmitted energy, at the frequencies that matter. Vibration is controlled by tool selection and trigger time in step 8
Safety boots to AS/NZS 2210.3
Hard hat to AS/NZS 1801 when working below others or in an EWP
Full body harness and lanyard to AS/NZS 1891.1:2007 in a boom-type EWP
Hi-vis to AS/NZS 4602.1 where powered mobile plant or traffic is present

steps.step: Get the asbestos register, the asbestos management plan and the drilling approval before you leave the branch
hazards: Building built before 1990 and no register sighted — you are drilling blind into fabric that may be asbestos cement
Register exists but was last reviewed before the refurbishment that put the ceiling in
Scope creep: the office quoted three detectors, the site wants twelve in a plant room nobody has ever inspected

controls.control: No register, no drill. If the person with management or control cannot produce an asbestos register for the building, the job does not start. The authority that ALWAYS applies is Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 427(2): where a PCBU carries out or intends to carry out work at a workplace that involves a risk of exposure to airborne asbestos, the person with management or control must ensure that PCBU is given a copy of the asbestos register. Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 425 requires a register to be prepared and kept for the workplace, and s 425(6) is the only escape — a building constructed after 31 December 1989 with no asbestos identified and none likely to be present from time to time. Where the scope is genuinely refurbishment — a fitout, a new riser, a slab cored for new pipework — part 8.6 also applies and s 449 and s 450 add a separate duty on the site to hand the register over and on Safe QLD to obtain it before we start. Do not lead with s 450 on a detector swap: s 447(2) provides that demolition or refurbishment does not include minor or routine maintenance work, or other minor work, and a site that knows the regulation will tell you so.

Read the register before you leave. Note every ACM entry within 5 m of a planned drill point, its recorded condition, and every area marked inaccessible or not inspected. Where the register calls an area inaccessible, the site must already be assuming asbestos is present (Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 422(2)(b)). Where it says the area was simply not inspected, no assumption arises in law and the Safe QLD rule fills the gap: not inspected is treated as asbestos.

Ask for the asbestos management plan as well as the register. Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 429 requires the person with management or control to have a written asbestos management plan wherever asbestos or ACM is identified at the workplace or is likely to be present from time to time, and s 429(4)(c) requires it to include procedures for incidents or emergencies involving asbestos. s 429(5) makes it readily accessible to you. It is the document that tells you the site's procedure for an unexpected find, for working around ACM, and who to call. Read the incident procedure before you start, not after you have cut something.

Confirm the construction date from the site, not from how the place looks. Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 447(1)(a) applies the demolition and refurbishment provisions to a building constructed before 31 December 1989 — that date is the trigger, and it is also the date in s 425(6).

Where there is no register at all, Safe QLD assumes the substrate is asbestos and does not drill. The site's duty to identify by a competent person, or to assume, is Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 422. If the scope is refurbishment, s 451 also requires the structure to be inspected by a competent person before work starts, and s 451(4) requires asbestos to be assumed where that person is on reasonable grounds uncertain, or where part of the structure is inaccessible and likely to be disturbed. Book the inspection, not the drill.

Scope growth re-triggers the written crystalline silica assessment and a review of this SWMS before the extra holes are drilled. Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 529CA(2)(d) makes the assessment turn on the likely frequency and duration of exposure, so twelve holes plus two cores is a different assessment from three holes; Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 302 requires this SWMS to be reviewed and revised when the control measures are revised. The assessment is per task and per shift, not per hole. Ring the supervisor before you agree to the extra work, not after.

steps.responsible: Safe QLD supervisor, with the site's person with management or control

steps.step: Walk every drill point against the register on arrival
hazards: Register says "ceiling lining, level 2" and the plant room ceiling above the FIP is a different sheet again
AC sheet used as the switchboard backing panel behind the fire panel — normal in pre-1980 plant rooms and rarely in the register
Vinyl floor tile and its black bitumen adhesive where you core the floor for pipework
Friable pipe lagging in the riser you are drilling beside
Painted, skimmed or flush-set AC sheet that defeats every visual tell on the list below

controls.control: Mark and photograph every drill point before anything is set up. A point that is not clearly on non-ACM substrate in the register does not get drilled today.

Look for the tells: 6 mm compressed sheet with a dimpled or brushed face, Super Six corrugated, tapered eaves sheeting, textured vermiculite ceilings, millboard behind heaters, Zelemite or Ausbestos switchboard panels, rope gasket in a fire door or damper.

Where the register calls an area inaccessible, the site must already be assuming asbestos is present under Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 422(2)(b) — that paragraph reaches a part of the workplace that is inaccessible to workers AND likely to contain asbestos or ACM. Where the register says the area was simply not inspected, s 422(2)(b) does not apply and there is no assumption in law, so the Safe QLD rule fills the gap: not inspected is treated as asbestos and you go straight to the stop step. Either way the duty to identify or assume sits on the person with management or control under s 422(1), and the duty to eliminate or minimise your exposure to airborne asbestos under s 420 sits on Safe QLD.

Check for the ACM label. Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 424 requires the presence and location of identified asbestos to be clearly indicated and, where reasonably practicable, labelled — if the label is there, the question is already answered and you do not drill it.

Be honest about what this walk-around is worth. You are not a competent person for asbestos identification, and Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 422(1) puts identification on one. Painted, skimmed or flush-set AC sheet routinely defeats the tells. The residual on this step is carried by the stop rule in step 7 and by the P2 being on your face before the bit goes in — not by the walk-around itself. Where you are not sure, it is asbestos.

steps.step: Design the penetration out before you make one
hazards: Drilling ACM when the fixing never had to go there
Coring a fresh hole through a fire-rated slab when an existing sleeve is 400 mm away

controls.control: Move the fixing. AS 1670.1 leaves you spacing tolerance on detector siting — use it to land the base on plasterboard, a steel purlin, a joist or the T-bar grid instead of AC sheet. Record the offset and the reason.
Use a penetration that already exists. Old cable sleeves, conduit stubs and abandoned riser holes save both a hole and a fire-stopping job.

Where the fixing must land near sound ACM sheet, use a stand-off bracket fixed to the framing behind it, or a proprietary grid clip, rather than putting a bit into the sheet — and without drilling, cutting, abrading or loading the sheet itself, and without a clearance hole through it. A 'small clearance hole' through AC sheet is still drilling asbestos. If the bracket cannot land clear of the sheet, the fixing moves or the job stops.

Get any detector offset agreed with the designer or certifier before you move it — the siting still has to satisfy AS 1670.1 and the fire engineer's spacing. Put the agreement in writing on the job before you drill.

steps.responsible: Fire technician, with the Safe QLD supervisor

steps.step: Prove what is behind the surface before the bit touches it
hazards: Concealed 240 V or submains cable in a wall chase or ceiling void — a strike through a rotary hammer is a fatality, not a tingle
Post-tensioned tendon in a suspended slab; cutting one releases stored energy and can fail the slab
Sprinkler pipe, gas line, hydraulic riser or comms behind the sheet
Reinforcement in the core path
Wet coring into a void that has not been sighted — water and conductive slurry tracking onto live equipment, into the ceiling space above a switchboard or the FIP, or into occupied space below

controls.control: Where a live circuit runs through the drill zone and cannot be avoided, do not drill until it is dead. The default answer on this job is isolation, not clever scanning. If the site will not isolate, the work does not proceed on a locator and a depth stop unless the Safe QLD supervisor authorises it in writing, on the day, on this SWMS — and in that case the residual risk for this step is HIGH, not medium, and you work it that way.

The site's licensed electrician performs the isolation at the board that feeds the area and proves dead at the point of work — Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 196 requires a competent person to test whether equipment is energised before work on or near it, and every exposed part is treated as energised until it is isolated and found not to be. You then fit your own personal danger lock and tag to the same isolation point and you keep the only key to it. Nobody removes your lock but you. The building manager does not hold a key to anything on that board. Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) ss 197 and 198 back this up: de-energised equipment must not be inadvertently re-energised, and where the isolating device is not under the worker's sole effective control it must be locked open and carry a warning sign.

No wet drilling or coring where a live circuit or energised equipment sits in, above or below the drill zone until it is isolated and proven dead. Water and diamond slurry are conductive. Bund and contain the slurry at the hole, sheet and protect any equipment below, catch the run-off at the wall or floor rather than letting it find a path, and never wet-core into a riser or void you have not physically sighted first. Step 8 makes wet coring mandatory above 25 mm — this is the control that stops that mandate drowning a switchboard.

Set a depth stop on the tool and check it against the fixing. A detector base fixing needs 35 to 40 mm, not 100 mm — most strikes are made by drilling deeper than the job required. The depth stop is the one control on this step that keeps working when everything else has been wrong.

RCD-protected supply to every portable tool, and the RCD tested on the day and the result logged. Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 140 requires all electrical equipment for the performance of construction work to comply with AS/NZS 3012 (Electrical installations — Construction and demolition sites), which is where the RCD requirement lives; safety switches are tested to AS/NZS 3760, and a portable one is tested by pushing its test button immediately after it is connected. An RCD is an engineering control — it interrupts fault current. It is not PPE and it will not save you from a rotary hammer through a submain.

Scan the full drill footprint with a cable and rebar locator, two passes at 90 degrees, before the bit touches the surface. A clear scan is not proof. It lowers the odds; it does not make the circuit safe. Locators have well-documented false negatives on deep cables, cables in steel conduit, screened cables and cables run tight against reinforcement. The only engineering control for a live cable in the drill zone is isolation.

For any core through a suspended slab, assume post-tension until the structural engineer of record confirms otherwise in writing. A cable and rebar locator will not reliably find tendons. GPR by a competent operator is the minimum, and it is a supplement to the engineer's drawings and mark-up, never a substitute. No engineer's mark-up, no core — and no coring at all inside a no-core zone the engineer nominates. Getting a document and running a survey is verification, not engineering: nothing about it stops a tendon letting go.

Connecting the device back to FIP wiring is electrical work under the Electrical Safety Act 2002 (Qld) — the licensed person does it, and AS/NZS 3000 applies to the cabling either way. Where that work has to be done on or near energised equipment, part 8 division 3 of the Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) applies: s 195 allows it only in the limited cases listed there, s 199 requires a recorded risk assessment and a separate energised-work safe work method statement before it starts, and 'near' means within 3 m of an exposed energised part.

steps.responsible: Fire technician, with the site's licensed electrician for isolation and the structural engineer of record for any slab core

steps.step: Isolate the detection system and put the building on notice
hazards: Drill dust and vibration puts a smoke detector into alarm and the brigade rolls
Zone left isolated with occupants inside and nobody told
Occupants walking through the dust, or dust reaching them through an open ceiling grid
HVAC shutdown itself raising smoke-mode faults at the FIP mid-job

controls.control: Isolate the affected zone or loop at the FIP, not the whole panel. Record the zone number and the time on the panel and in the log.
Put the ASE and the brigade connection on test with the monitoring provider, get a reference number, and set a call-back time.
Hard barricade and signage at every approach. Nobody who has not signed this SWMS crosses it.

Contain the work area, not just the approach. Poly drop sheet or a dust screen at the ceiling opening, tiles kept closed except at the point of work, and the void sealed off from the rest of the floor — drilling above an open grid in a live office, ward or aged-care wing is a direct path from the void into occupied space. In a hospital, day surgery or aged-care facility, get the site's infection control risk assessment and interim life safety measures before the day. The containment class they set governs, and it is stricter than this SWMS.

The site's BMS operator or mechanical services contractor shuts down the HVAC serving the work area, or at least the return air, so dust is not distributed through the building and into other detectors. This is not a control a fire technician can apply — arrange it as a line on the impairment permit before the day, not on the spot, and confirm with them whether the shutdown will raise smoke-mode faults at the FIP so you are not chasing your own faults all morning.
Tell the building's fire safety adviser and the chief warden that detection in that area is off, and agree the interim measure — normally a posted fire watch or the area cleared.

Put a time limit on the impairment and write it on the permit. Name the warden or fire watch and record their name and mobile. If the isolation will cross a shift, a break or a lunch, hand it over in writing to a named person and record the handover. If the work will not finish inside the agreed window, restore detection and re-isolate tomorrow rather than running the building unprotected overnight.

steps.responsible: Fire technician, with the site's fire safety adviser and the site's BMS operator or mechanical services contractor

steps.step: Set up the access to the ceiling
hazards: Fall above 2 m with both hands on a rotary hammer overhead
Drill snatch or bit bind pushing you off the platform
Dropped drill or core barrel onto people below
Core plug drops through the slab into the space below as the cut breaks through
Core barrel binds and the drill stand lets go — an unanchored stand overhead is a projectile
EWP driven into sprinkler heads or services
Technician suspended in a harness with nobody on site to reach the ground controls

controls.control: Do the assembly on the deck. Terminate the base, dress the tails and set the depth stop at ground level so the time overhead is drilling only.

Barricade the drop zone below and keep it clear. Tool lanyards on the drill, the bit and the base. For a slab core, barricade, sign and post a spotter in the space BELOW the slab, not only the room you are standing in, and keep it manned for the final 10 mm of the cut.

Work off a platform with guardrails — scissor lift, mobile scaffold or a platform ladder with a handrail. A rotary hammer overhead off a leaning A-frame is not a control, and Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 299(4) makes you describe in this SWMS every control you considered, including the general fall protection requirements in s 79, if administrative controls or PPE are all you are going to implement. A mobile scaffold with a working platform from which a person or object could fall more than 4 m is scaffolding work under Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) schedule 19 — it is erected, altered and dismantled only by the holder of a basic scaffolding high risk work licence (schedule 3). Below 4 m, erect it to the manufacturer's instructions, brace it, lock the castors and never move it with a person or tools on the deck.
Side handle fitted and a clutch-equipped drill, so a bind spins the tool instead of you.

Mechanically restrain or capture the core before break-through — a plug strap, a core catcher, or a barrel that holds the plug. Anchor the drill stand with a bolt, or use a vacuum base with a working vacuum-loss alarm. Never a jack-stand alone for overhead or near-vertical work.

A boom-type EWP is never operated with a harness unless a second competent person is on site, briefed on the ground controls, and in continuous line of sight or radio contact. A written rescue plan for suspension is on the job before the basket leaves the ground, and it has been practised — Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 80 requires the emergency and rescue procedures for a fall arrest system to be established, tested so that they are effective, and trained. No second person, no boom lift: use a scissor lift, a mobile scaffold or a platform, or reschedule.

High risk work licence class WP for an operator of a boom-type elevating work platform with a boom length of 11 m or more (Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) schedule 3); operator familiarisation and a current Yellow Card under 11 m. Pre-start the machine and log it. Walk the travel path for sprinkler heads and services before you raise anything.
In a boom-type EWP, full harness and lanyard to AS/NZS 1891.1:2007 anchored to the designated point in the basket. Not in a scissor lift unless the manufacturer's manual calls for it.

steps.responsible: Fire technician, with a second competent person on the ground for any boom-type EWP work

steps.step: You cut into it and it is, or might be, asbestos — stop
hazards: Fibro dust released into a ceiling void that feeds the whole floor
Technician pressing on because it is "only a small hole"
Contaminated tools, boots, hoses, vacuum and clothing carried to the next job
Friable material — lagging, vermiculite, millboard — routed to the wrong licence class and the wrong contractor called

controls.control: Stop the tool and stop the job. Safe QLD does not put a bit into asbestos. Start with Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 419(1): a PCBU must not carry out, or direct or allow a worker to carry out, work involving asbestos — and s 419(2) makes 'work involving asbestos' include handling or disturbing asbestos or ACM — unless the work falls in an s 419(3) exception. A new penetration for new equipment is not plainly 'maintenance of, or service work on' that ACM under s 419(3)(c). Even where an exception applies, s 446(3) and (4) mean no power tool touches it unless the equipment is enclosed during use, or is designed to capture or suppress airborne asbestos and is used that way. Drilling AC sheet also makes asbestos-contaminated dust, which s 486 only lets you handle unlicensed where it is minor contamination not associated with a removal. The licence thresholds are a separate question again, and the company rule sits above all of them. It goes to a licensed removalist under a removal control plan, or the fixing moves.
Barricade the area and have the HVAC serving it shut down. Nobody back in until it has been assessed. Leave the tool, the bit and the debris exactly where they are.

Do not withdraw the bit spinning, do not blow the hole clear, and do not brush it. Step back and leave everything where it is. This is emergency response, not elimination — the dust that has been released is already in the void, and nothing you do now takes it back.

Route it to the right licence class, because getting this wrong puts the wrong contractor on the job. FRIABLE — pipe and boiler lagging, sprayed limpet, vermiculite ceilings, millboard, or any AC sheet so degraded it crumbles under hand pressure — is class A asbestos removal work under Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 485 at any quantity, however small, with no area threshold. It needs a class A licensed removalist, air monitoring during the work by the holder of an asbestos assessor licence (s 489), a clearance inspection by an independent licensed asbestos assessor (s 473(2)(a)) and a clearance certificate before the area is reoccupied (s 474). NON-FRIABLE sheet in sound condition needs a class B licence above 10m² (s 487). If you are not certain which you are looking at, it is friable until a competent person says otherwise.

Prohibited on the spot by Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 446(1): no high-pressure water spray and no compressed air on asbestos or ACM. No broom either — s 446(3) catches brooms and any other implement that releases airborne asbestos.

Tell the site's person with management or control and the Safe QLD supervisor the same hour. Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 426 requires the asbestos register to be reviewed and, as necessary, revised where further asbestos or ACM is identified, or where asbestos is disturbed — your find goes into it, in writing.

If a sample is needed, a competent person takes it. Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 423(2) requires the sample to be analysed only by a NATA-accredited laboratory accredited for the relevant test method, a laboratory approved by the regulator, or one operated by the regulator, and the method for identification in bulk samples is AS 4964:2004. You do not scrape a sample into a snap-lock bag.

Decontaminate the tools before they leave the area — H-class vacuum then wet wipe the drill, the barrel, the bits, the hoses, the lanyards, the stand and the basket floor. Anything porous that cannot be cleaned is bagged as waste. The H-class vacuum is never emptied on site or in the ute, and its filter is changed only under controlled conditions by someone trained to do it. Boots wiped and coveralls bagged before you cross the barricade, not at the ute.

The P2 was already on your face, fit-checked, before the bit went in. That is exactly why the dust controls in step 8 apply to every drill, not only the ones you expected to be dirty. If it was not on your face, say so now and record it — that is an exposure, and it is reported, not hidden.

steps.responsible: Fire technician, escalating to the Safe QLD supervisor and the site's person with management or control

steps.step: Drill and core concrete, brick, block and render
hazards: Respirable crystalline silica — concrete, mortar, brick and render all contain at least 1% crystalline silica by weight, so they are crystalline silica substances, and a power tool drilling them is "processing" under Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 529A
Overhead drilling drops the dust straight onto your face and inside the mask seal
Dry core drilling a slab
Hand-arm vibration from a week of rotary hammering and coring — cumulative, career-ending, and invisible until it is permanent
Respirator that no longer seals — lapsed fit test, wrong model issued, or a beard grown since the last one

controls.control: On-tool extraction — shrouded bit into an H-class HEPA vacuum matched to the tool — or effective wet suppression. Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 529C makes controlled processing the only lawful way to do it, and s 529B(1)(b) lists what counts as a control measure: isolation of a person from dust exposure, a fully enclosed operator cabin with high efficiency air filtration, an effective wet dust suppression method, an effective on-tool extraction system, or an effective local exhaust ventilation system. At least one of them must be in use during the processing.

Wet core drilling with a water feed and slurry ring for anything over 25 mm diameter — subject to the wet coring hold in step 4, which comes first: nothing wet goes into a void with live equipment in, above or below it until that equipment is isolated and proven dead. Slurry is picked up with a wet vac, not squeegeed down the riser or the floor waste.

Control vibration at the tool, because gloves will not. Select tools on their declared vibration emission (m/s²) and use the lowest that will do the work. Keep bits sharp and correct for the substrate — a blunt bit doubles both the time and the energy going into your hands. Use the drill stand for coring rather than hand-holding the rig, and let the tool do the work rather than pushing on it.

The written crystalline silica assessment is done before the processing starts and recorded in writing (Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 529CA(1) and (4)). It is made without regard to PPE or administrative controls (s 529CA(3)), and it must not rely solely on the effect of the on-tool extraction or wet suppression you intend to use (s 529CA(1A)). If you cannot make the determination, the processing is taken to be reasonably likely to result in a risk to health (s 529CA(5)) and is therefore high risk (s 529BA(b)).

This SWMS IS the silica risk control plan for this work, and it only stays that way if it is kept honest. High risk processing needs a silica risk control plan under Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 529CB(1), but s 529CB(3) removes that duty where the processing is also high risk construction work, a SWMS is prepared before the processing starts, and the SWMS satisfies s 529CB(2). To satisfy s 529CB(2) this document (a) identifies the high risk processing — drilling and coring concrete, brick, block, mortar and render; (b) carries the s 529CA assessment for the job as Annexure A, attached to and forming part of this SWMS BEFORE the first hole, not filed after; and (c) states how the controls are implemented, monitored and reviewed, which is also what Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 299(2)(d) requires. HOW THEY ARE MONITORED AND REVIEWED: the extraction, vacuum filter and water feed are checked at pre-start and signed off on the job card; the supervisor spot-checks one job in five on site; any control that fails stops the processing until it is fixed; and the assessment and this SWMS are re-done when the scope grows, the substrate changes, air monitoring comes back, or a control is revised (s 302 and s 529CC(3)). If Annexure A is not attached, s 529CB(3) does not apply and a separate silica risk control plan is required before you drill.

Where the assessment cannot rule out that the airborne concentration is more than half the exposure standard (Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 529CA(2)(e)), arrange respirable crystalline silica air monitoring on a representative shift. Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 50 requires air monitoring where you are not certain on reasonable grounds whether the exposure standard is exceeded, s 50(2) requires the results to be kept for 30 years and made accessible, and s 49 requires that nobody is exposed above the standard. Feed the results back into the next assessment under s 529CA(2)(f). Where the processing is determined to be high risk, health monitoring for the workers doing it is arranged through the Safe QLD supervisor before they start.

Before the first hole, the respirator gate: confirm your fit test is current and is for the exact make, model and size of respirator you are wearing today; confirm you are clean-shaven at the seal; and do a positive and negative fit check every time you don it. Any one of those fails and the drilling does not start. A P2 on a beard is decoration. The same gate applies to step 7 — the mask has to be sealing before you find the asbestos, not after.

Track trigger time across the shift, not the job. Set a daily trigger-time limit from the tool's declared vibration emission before you start, break up long coring runs, and rotate the drilling between technicians where the day is heavy. Report tingling, numbness or blanching in the fingers to the supervisor — it does not get better on its own.
No dry cutting, no dry sweeping, no compressed air to clear the hole. The hole gets vacuumed.

P2 half-face minimum, fit-tested, per AS/NZS 1715:2009 and AS/NZS 1716:2012 — the editions Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 529B(3) names. The exposure standard for respirable crystalline silica is currently 0.05 mg/m³ as an 8-hour time-weighted average in the Workplace Exposure Standard for Airborne Contaminants, which is the instrument Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) schedule 19 points to; check the current figure in that instrument before you rely on it, because the exposure standards list is under revision. You cannot see it being exceeded, which is why the engineering controls above are not optional.

steps.responsible: Fire technician, with the Safe QLD supervisor for the written assessment, air monitoring and health monitoring

steps.step: Drill through painted surfaces in an older building
hazards: Lead paint — Australian paint ran above 1% lead into the mid-1960s and above 0.25% until 1992, so old painted steel, joinery, plant room walls and handrails are all candidates. The regulatory trigger in Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 392(h) and (o) is paint containing MORE THAN 1% lead by dry weight
Sanding or grinding the paint back to seat a base plate flat, which is what turns the job into a lead process

controls.control: Do not sand, disc, grind or buff painted surfaces to seat a fixing, and do not power-tool paint off to make a plate sit. That is what makes it a lead process under Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 392(h) (machine sanding or buffing surfaces coated with paint containing more than 1% lead by dry weight) and s 392(o) (using a power tool to remove a surface coated with such paint, and handling the waste). Use a packer, a stand-off or a larger backing plate.
Shadow-vac the bit with the same H-class vacuum used for the silica step, with a damp cloth or shroud under the drill point to catch what falls.

Know which side of 1% you are on before you talk about lead processes. Paint between 0.25% and 1% lead is still a hazardous chemical to be managed under chapter 7 and the exposure standard still applies, but it does not by itself make the job a lead process. Where the lead content is unknown and the paint predates 1970, work to the lead process rules until it is tested.

If the paint is flaking or the plate cannot sit without preparation, stop and refer it to the supervisor. A lead process requires the health risk information under Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 395 to be given before the worker commences it. Whether it is lead risk work is assessed under s 402, that assessment disregards the effect of PPE (s 402(3)), and if the PCBU is unable to determine whether lead risk work is carried out, the process is taken to include lead risk work until it is determined otherwise (s 402(4)). Lead risk work then requires written notice to the regulator within 7 days (s 403(1)) and health monitoring before the worker first commences it and again one month after (s 405(1)).
Wet-wipe the surrounds and the floor before you pack up. Lead dust left on a plant room floor is the next person's exposure.

P2 stays on. The inorganic lead dust and fume exposure standard is currently 0.05 mg/m³ as an 8-hour time-weighted average in the Workplace Exposure Standard for Airborne Contaminants — check the current figure in that instrument before you rely on it. Wash hands before eating, drinking or smoking — lead goes in through the mouth as much as the lungs.

steps.responsible: Fire technician, escalating to the Safe QLD supervisor before any paint is prepared or removed

steps.step: Clean up before you come off the platform
hazards: Dust left in the ceiling void, on the T-bar and on top of the diffusers, waiting for the next trade to disturb it
Shop vac without HEPA blowing fine dust back into the room at head height
Contaminated coveralls and boots carried to the next site and into the ute

controls.control: Asbestos waste and contaminated PPE is double-bagged in 200 µm polythene, gooseneck sealed, labelled, and taken to a facility licensed under the Environmental Protection Act 1994 (Qld). It does not go in the site skip and it does not ride loose in the ute.
H-class HEPA vacuum only, filter in date and logged. A domestic or standard workshop vac makes the exposure worse, not better, because it puts the fine fraction back into the room at head height.

Vacuum first, then wet-wipe. Never sweep and never blow it clear — Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 446(1) prohibits compressed air and high-pressure water spray on asbestos, s 446(3) catches brooms, and it is indefensible on silica and lead as well.
Vacuum the tile, the grid and the top face of the sheet before the tile goes back, plus the cable tray and the top of any diffuser within reach of the drill point.

Before the tile goes back, do and record a visual clearance of the void within reach of the drill point — no visible dust or debris on the top face of the sheet, the grid, the tray or the diffuser. Photograph it onto the job. If you cannot see into the void to check it, say so in the job notes for the next trade and leave the residual at medium: an unverified clean is not a clean.
Coveralls come off last, vacuumed down before removal and bagged on the spot. Not shaken out, not worn to the next job, not taken home. Boots wiped before they cross the barricade.

steps.step: Make the penetration good
hazards: A cored hole through a fire-rated wall or slab left open or packed with loose rockwool, defeating the compartment for the life of the building
Cut edge of ACM left raw where an authorised penetration was made
Base mounted and the ceiling tile left out of the grid

controls.control: Fire-stop with a tested and approved system for that FRL, that substrate and that service — the system's own tested detail, not a tube of generic sealant. AS 4072.1 and AS 1530.4 govern the test evidence, and the National Construction Code sets the required FRL. If you do not have the tested detail on the job, do not improvise it: leave the penetration protected and get the detail.
Photograph the penetration before and after, and record product, batch and installer. If the certifier cannot see the evidence, it did not happen.

Where a penetration in ACM was authorised and made by the licensed removalist, the cut edge is sealed with a compatible sealant by them, and the location and condition are written back into the asbestos register under Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 426.
Reinstate the grid, the tile and any smoke seal you disturbed, and check the detector siting against AS 1670.1 before the tile goes back.

steps.responsible: Fire technician, with the fire-stopping installer where a certified system is used

steps.step: Return the system to service and write down what you disturbed
hazards: Zone left isolated overnight and the building unprotected
Monitoring left on test and a real alarm not transmitted
Nobody records that the plant room ceiling was drilled, or what it turned out to be

controls.control: De-isolate every zone you isolated, at the panel, before you leave site. Walk the FIP and confirm normal, with no residual faults or isolations left showing. This is a mandatory end-of-job verification, not a hierarchy control — nothing here removes a hazard, it only catches the one you created this morning.

Take the ASE off test with the monitoring provider, get confirmation and record the reference. Test one device on the restored zone and confirm receipt at the monitoring centre — end to end, not just at the panel.
Record it in the AS 1851 log: what was isolated, when, by whom, when restored, and the functional test result on the new device.

Report any asbestos find, sample result or authorised disturbance in writing to the person with management or control, so the register is reviewed and revised under Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 426 and the asbestos management plan under s 430.

Attach the drill point photographs, Annexure A (the written silica assessment) and the signed SWMS to the job before you close it. Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 303 requires this SWMS to be kept until the work is complete, and for at least 2 years if a notifiable incident occurred in connection with it.

steps.responsible: Fire technician, with the Safe QLD supervisor

emergency:
SUSPECTED ASBESTOS DISTURBANCE. Stop the tool, leave it where it is, and do not brush, sweep or blow anything. Get everyone out and tape the area off, have the HVAC serving it shut down, and keep your respirator and coveralls on until you are outside the area — then vacuum down, bag the coveralls on the spot and wash. Call the site contact and the Safe QLD supervisor the same hour. The site arranges a competent person or licensed assessor to assess and clean; nobody re-enters until they clear it, and after class A work that clearance is a certificate under the regulation, not a verbal all-clear. Write it up the same day and give it to the person with management or control so the asbestos register gets revised. NOTIFICATION, precisely: an uncontrolled release of asbestos is an uncontrolled escape of a substance and is a dangerous incident under Work Health and Safety Act 2011 (Qld) s 37(a), which makes it a notifiable incident under s 35 — call Workplace Health and Safety Queensland on 1300 362 128 immediately, by the fastest possible means (s 38). Separately, if a person requires medical treatment within 48 hours of the exposure, that is a serious injury or illness under s 36(c) and is notifiable in its own right. Either way s 39 requires the site of the incident to be preserved until an inspector arrives or directs otherwise.

CABLE STRIKE OR ELECTRIC SHOCK. Do not touch the person or the tool. Kill the supply at the board you locked, or the main switch if you cannot reach it. Call 000. Treat for burns at both entry and exit, and get the person assessed even if they walked away — a shock through the chest can kill hours later. The circuit stays isolated and out of service until a licensed electrician clears it. Electric shock is a dangerous incident under Work Health and Safety Act 2011 (Qld) s 37(e): call WHSQ on 1300 362 128 and do not disturb the scene.

FALL FROM THE PLATFORM OR THE EWP. Do not move the person unless they are in immediate danger. Call 000. If someone is hanging in a harness, this is urgent — get them out of suspension inside 10 to 15 minutes and keep them sitting up, not laid flat. The second person lowers the basket from the ground controls if the operator is incapacitated; that is why step 6 does not let a boom lift leave the ground without them. A fall, or the release from a height of any plant, substance or thing, is a dangerous incident under Work Health and Safety Act 2011 (Qld) s 37(f) — make the call and leave the plant and the scene as they are.

FIRST AID COVER. A current HLTAID011 first aider is on site for the duration of the work, not merely employed by the company. If the only first aider leaves, the drilling stops until they are back or another one arrives.

WORKING ALONE. Do not drill overhead, core, or work off any platform alone. Where any part of this work is unavoidably solo — and it must not be the overhead, coring or platform part — agree a check-in interval with the Safe QLD supervisor before you start, and an escalation if you miss one: who calls, who attends, and who has the site address and access details. A missed check-in is treated as an incident until proven otherwise.

DUST OR SWARF IN THE EYE. Eyewash for a full 15 minutes, hold the lid open, do not rub and do not try to pick anything out. Straight to a doctor, and take the SDS or a photo of the material with you.

FIRE WHILE THE SYSTEM IS ISOLATED. The detection in that area is off and it is not going to call anybody. Raise the alarm by voice, call 000 yourself, then de-isolate the FIP and take the ASE off test. Do not wait until you get to the panel to make the call.

CUTTING A POST-TENSIONED TENDON. Stop, clear everyone from under and around the slab immediately, and do not cut, drill or load anything further. Call the structural engineer and the site contact before anyone goes back under it. A collapse or partial collapse of a structure is a dangerous incident under Work Health and Safety Act 2011 (Qld) s 37(h).

Does the register cover the exact ceiling void, wall, riser and slab you are drilling, or is that area listed as inaccessible or not inspected?
Which FIP is it, where is it, which zone or loop covers the work area, and who holds the key?
Who is the monitoring provider, and what account or reference number do you quote to put the ASE on test?
What time limit is on the impairment permit, who is the named fire watch, and what is their mobile?
Who shuts down the HVAC serving the work area — BMS operator or mechanical contractor — and will the shutdown raise smoke-mode faults at the FIP?
Which distribution board feeds the wall or ceiling you are drilling, where is it, and which licensed electrician will isolate it and prove it dead so you can fit your own lock?
Is the wall, floor or slab you are coring fire-rated, what FRL, and who approves the penetration?
Is the slab post-tensioned, who is the structural engineer of record, and where is their mark-up and any no-core zone?
Who is the second person on site for boom-type EWP work, are they briefed on the ground controls, and how will you stay in contact?
Is your respirator fit test current, for this exact make, model and size, and are you clean-shaven at the seal today?
Where is the H-class vacuum, is its filter in date, and where is the nearest water point for wet suppression? Where does the slurry go?
Has silica air monitoring been done for this class of work, and does the assessment need it before this job?
Where does asbestos waste go from this site, and who is licensed to transport it?

Is this a hospital, day surgery or aged-care facility, and where is the infection control risk assessment and the interim life safety measures approval?
Who is the site contact, and what is their mobile, if you find unexpected ACM and have to stop mid-job?
Where is the assembly area, the nearest first aid kit and eyewash, who is the HLTAID011 first aider on site today, and what is the site emergency number?

title: Confined space entry — fire water tanks, pump wells, pits and risers
activity: Entering a confined space to inspect or service fire protection plant: fire water tank internals, pump wet wells, below-ground valve and booster pits, and sealed riser shafts.
