title: Electrical Work — Fire System Wiring, Panels, Batteries and Mains Supply
activity: Electrical work on fire detection and suppression systems: isolating and proving dead, working inside fire indicator panels with 240 V present, energised testing where it genuinely cannot be avoided, replacing battery banks, running and terminating cable to the Wiring Rules, and work on the submain feeding a fire pump.

hrcw.clause: Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld), s 291(k)
hrcw.text: is carried out on or near energised electrical installations or services

whenRequired:
WHEN YOU NEED THIS SWMS. Any time you will have the cover off something carrying 240 V or more — a fire indicator panel, an ASE, an EWIS or occupant warning rack, a switchboard, a fire pump controller — or you are cutting, replacing or terminating cable, or changing out a battery bank. You do not need it to press TEST at the panel front, walk a building with a smoke tester, or read battery volts off the display.

IS IT CONSTRUCTION WORK? START FROM YES. Maintenance and testing of a fire system is construction work: Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 289(2)(e) captures 'the installation, testing or maintenance of an essential service in relation to a structure', and a fire detection and alarm system is an essential service. Work only falls out of Chapter 6 if it is genuinely 'testing, maintenance or repair work of a minor nature carried out in connection with a structure' (s 289(3)(d)) — and that is a call made job by job, not a blanket exemption for routine AS 1851 service. If you have the cover off, assume it is construction work and this SWMS applies. And note there is no no-paperwork path either way: Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 199 independently requires a recorded risk assessment and a safe work method statement before ANY electrical work on or near energised electrical equipment, whether or not the job is construction work.

WHAT 'NEAR' MEANS. 'Near' is not a matter of judgement. Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 193 defines it: near, in relation to electrical equipment, means within 3 m of an exposed energised part of the equipment. Once the FIP door is open with the mains terminal block, transformer or charger exposed, everyone standing inside that 3 m is in energised electrical work and Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) ss 199-204 apply to them — not just to the person with hands in the panel. That includes a second technician, an apprentice, and the building manager who came to watch.

WHAT THIS SWMS DOES NOT COVER. The high risk construction work this statement covers is Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 291(k) — work carried out on or near energised electrical installations or services. If the same job also involves any of the following, each is a separate high risk construction work category in its own right: a risk of falling more than 2 m (s 291(a)); disturbance of asbestos (s 291(d)); work in or near a confined space such as a pump room pit, tank or valve pit (s 291(f)); or work in an area that may have a contaminated or flammable atmosphere, including a vented (flooded) cell battery room (s 291(l)). Hot work is covered by its own permit and SWMS. Add the matching SWMS. Do not stretch this one over them.

WHO IS A SAFETY OBSERVER. Safety observer means a person who meets the definition in Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) schedule 10 — competent to implement control measures in an emergency or to avoid an emergency, competent to rescue and resuscitate a worker carrying out the work if necessary, and assessed in the previous 12 months as competent to rescue and resuscitate a person. The observer observes the work and does nothing else. A second pair of hands is not a safety observer. An apprentice is not a safety observer. A fire technician without an electrical background is not a safety observer. An observer is not required only where the work consists only of testing AND the recorded s 199(1)(a) risk assessment shows there is no serious risk associated with the proposed work (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 203(3)).

WHO IS AUTHORISED. Energised electrical work is performed only by workers named on Safe QLD's current list of workers authorised to perform energised electrical work, held with this SWMS on the job cover sheet. The technician does not self-certify. Authorisation for a particular job is given by the Safe QLD supervisor after consulting the person with management or control of the workplace — the building manager or occupier (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 199(1)(e)).

HOW RISK IS RATED IN THIS DOCUMENT (the Safe QLD 5 x 5 matrix). CONSEQUENCE: Catastrophic — fatality or permanent disability (electrocution, arc blast, fall from height, an unprotected building that burns). Major — serious injury needing hospital admission (arc flash burns, a shock with cardiac effects). Moderate — injury needing medical treatment and lost time (a burn, a crush, a strain). Minor — first aid only. Insignificant — no injury. LIKELIHOOD: Almost certain — expected on most jobs of this type. Likely — will probably occur at some point. Possible — could occur. Unlikely — could occur but not expected. Rare — only in exceptional circumstances. BANDS: EXTREME — catastrophic or major consequence at possible likelihood or higher; work does not start without the full control set applied and verified. HIGH — catastrophic or major consequence at unlikely likelihood, or moderate at likely or higher; supervisor authorisation required, work does not proceed on the technician's own authority. MEDIUM — moderate consequence at possible or lower, or minor at likely or higher; proceed with the controls applied and the step monitored. LOW — minor or insignificant consequence at unlikely or lower; proceed. Every initialRisk in this document is the rating BEFORE the controls in that step; every residualRisk is the rating with all of those controls actually applied — not with them merely written down.

HOW THE CONTROLS ARE IMPLEMENTED, MONITORED AND REVIEWED (Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 299(2)(d) and Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 200(d)). IMPLEMENTED: by the person named in 'responsible' for each step, in the order the steps are written, with the site-specific questions answered on site before the first cover comes off. MONITORED: (1) before work starts, the lead technician confirms on the job card that every worker has signed on to this SWMS and that the site matches the plan; (2) the isolation is independently confirmed by a second worker, who initials the job card, before any cover comes off; (3) during energised work the safety observer confirms — and keeps confirming — that barriers are in place, that the isolation point is clear and reachable, that tools and instruments are in test date, and that nobody unauthorised has come inside the barrier; (4) fire-stopping, cable support and segregation are checked and photographed by a second person before anything is covered; (5) at handback the lead technician verifies against this statement that every isolation made has been removed, every disturbed device tested, and the pumpset proved running. REVIEWED: this SWMS is reviewed and, as necessary, revised whenever the relevant control measures are revised under Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 38 (s 302), and in any case on the first of — a notifiable incident, a serious electrical incident, a dangerous electrical event or a near miss on this work; a change of panel platform, switchboard or site conditions; a change in the law or in a standard this statement relies on; a worker raising a concern about any control in it; or twelve months from the date it was prepared. A revised statement is re-signed by every worker before work resumes under it.

STOP WORK. If any control in this SWMS cannot be applied as written, the work stops immediately, or as soon as it is safe to do so, and resumes only in accordance with this statement (Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 300(2)). A residual risk of HIGH is not a licence to proceed — it means the work does not go ahead on the technician's own authority. It goes back to the supervisor, and if the residual cannot be brought below high, the work is not done energised. Any worker on this job may stop it, at any time, for any safety reason, without consequence of any kind.

VERSION, SIGN-ON AND RETENTION. The job cover sheet carried with this statement records: version number and date prepared; who prepared it; the workers consulted in preparing it; the list of workers authorised to perform energised electrical work; and the worker sign-on table (name, licence number, signature, date) which every worker on the job completes before starting and completes again if this statement is revised. Where the work is high risk construction work in connection with a construction project, a copy goes to the principal contractor before the work commences (Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 301). RETENTION: keep this SWMS until the work it relates to is complete, and for at least 2 years after a notifiable incident occurring in connection with that work (Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 303). For energised electrical work, keep the recorded risk assessment for at least 28 days after the work is completed and this SWMS until the work is completed, and keep both for at least 2 years if a serious electrical incident or dangerous electrical event occurs in connection with the work (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 204). A copy stays readily accessible to every worker on the job and available for inspection.
permits: Fire system impairment / out-of-service permit — ASE isolation reference from the monitoring provider and the AS 1851 log book entry, before any work starts

Electrical isolation permit with personal lock and danger tag (lock-out tag-out), one lock per worker. The tag is a warning sign attached to the isolating device in a prominent position and suitable in the circumstances, having regard to AS 1319 (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 198(2)(a))

Energised electrical work authorisation — recorded before the work starts, naming which exception in Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 195(1) is relied on and why; supported by the recorded risk assessment required by s 199(1)(a) and a SWMS complying with s 200; authorised by the Safe QLD supervisor after consulting the person with management or control of the workplace (s 199(1)(e))
Site contractor access / permit to work from the building manager, including after-hours access to plant rooms and risers
Fire pump impairment notice to the occupier where the pumpset submain is being isolated

Site asbestos register and asbestos management plan sighted before any drilling, cutting or fixing into an existing wall, floor, ceiling or panel backing board. No register is a stop. Where asbestos-containing material will be disturbed, that work leaves this SWMS and goes to a separate asbestos SWMS, and to a licensed removalist where the work is licensed asbestos removal work
Confined space entry permit — only if the pump room, tank or valve pit is classified as a confined space (separate SWMS applies)
Hot work permit to AS 1674.1 — only if brazing, grinding or soldering forms part of the job (separate SWMS applies)
Flammable atmosphere / vented battery room permit and SWMS — only if the battery bank is vented (flooded) cells or sits in a dedicated battery room. Vented cells are out of scope of this SWMS
ppe: Arc-rated (ATPV rated) long-sleeve shirt and trousers with an ATPV not less than the incident energy determined for the board or panel you are working at. Safe QLD's PPE schedule sets a minimum rating for fire indicator panel work and a higher minimum for main switchboard and fire pump controller work — check it before you leave the yard. If the incident energy at that board has not been determined, it is not opened live. No polyester, and no synthetic-mesh hi-vis vest worn over arc-rated clothing

Class 0 (1000 V) insulating gloves with leather overgloves for any work on or near exposed live parts. Electrically retested at the interval Safe QLD's PPE schedule requires and within the retest date marked on the glove; visually inspected and roll (air) tested by the wearer immediately before every use. A glove with no legible date does not go on
Arc-rated face shield plus arc-rated balaclava at switchboards, fire pump controllers and battery terminals
Clear safety glasses to AS/NZS 1337.1 worn under the face shield and at all times in the plant room
Safety footwear to AS/NZS 2210.3 of a non-conductive / electrically insulating classification. Footwear is a backstop, never a primary shock control — it does not make it safe to touch anything
Nitrile chemical gloves and face shield when handling batteries; eyewash or clean running water confirmed within reach before the first terminal nut is loosened
Hearing protection in the pump room whenever the pumpset may run
Hard hat where there is fixed plant, pipework or a riser overhead
Rated, in-date, dry insulating mat to stand on at any panel or board being worked on with parts energised
Insulated 1000 V hand tools to AS IEC 60900 (tools are not PPE, but they are non-negotiable on this job, and they are in test date and inspected before use)
training: Electrical work licence (electrical mechanic) issued under the Electrical Safety Act 2002 (Qld) by the Electrical Safety Office, and the business holding a current electrical contractor licence
QBCC fire protection occupational licence for the class of work — electrical, install and maintain, fire alarm systems; or fire detection, alarm and warning systems, maintain, extra low voltage

All workers who perform, or help in performing, electrical work: competent in rescue and resuscitation in accordance with recognised practices in the electricity industry (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 211). Note that s 211 sets no time period of its own

Safety observer: competent to implement control measures in an emergency or to avoid an emergency, competent to rescue and resuscitate a worker carrying out the work if necessary, and assessed in the previous 12 months as competent to rescue and resuscitate a person (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) schedule 10, definition of safety observer, paragraph (a)). The 12-month assessment is the observer's legal requirement

COMPANY RULE (not a legal requirement, and stated as company policy): Safe QLD refreshes low voltage rescue and CPR every 12 months for every worker who performs energised electrical work, not only for those acting as safety observer
Named on Safe QLD's current list of workers authorised to perform energised electrical work
Construction induction card (white card) where the work is construction work
Asbestos awareness training for every worker who drills, cuts or fixes into an existing structure
AS 1851 routine service competency and familiarity with the specific panel platform on site (Vigilant MX1/F4000, Ampac FireFinder, Pertronic F220, Kentec Taktis, Notifier)
Test instrument competency — voltage indicators, insulation resistance and loop impedance testers, with instruments in calibration/test date
Working at heights and EWP ticket where a platform or ladder above 2 m is used to reach cable, panels or EWIS equipment
Confined space entry training to AS 2865 where the plant room, tank or pit is classified as a confined space

steps.step: Plan the job before you leave the vehicle — scope, panel type, isolation points, who needs to know
hazards: Isolating the wrong circuit and dropping a tenancy, a lift or a switchboard you did not intend
Arriving without the panel manual or as-builts and improvising inside live gear
Working alone on a live panel with nobody to raise the alarm
Building occupants and the chief warden not knowing the system is about to go down
Energised, switchboard or battery work bolted onto the end of a full day — fatigue, on the job that punishes it hardest
Turning up without knowing whether the board has an arc flash study, a fault level label, or an asbestos register behind it
Your own extension leads, task light and power tools run off site supply with no RCD and no test tag

controls.control: Default is de-energised. If the job can be done with the system dead, it is booked and done dead — the live hazard is removed, not managed. Energised work is planned only where an exception in Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 195(1) genuinely applies, is written down, and is authorised before the crew leaves.
Portable equipment, extension leads and task lighting run off site supply are supplied through an RCD. If the outlet you are given is not RCD protected, use the portable RCD off the vehicle.
Ask the question and write the answer on the job card: can this whole job be done dead? Do not plan energised work to suit a schedule, a tenancy, or a client who does not want the noise.

Read the site's AS 1851 log book and last service record. Confirm the panel make and model — Vigilant MX1/F4000, Ampac FireFinder, Pertronic F220, Kentec Taktis, Notifier — and have that manual on the tablet before you open it. Get the switchboard schedule and the as-builts for the board that feeds it as well — if the schedule is thirty years old, plan on proving the circuit rather than trusting the label.

Ring the site contact and the chief warden before you leave the yard. Nobody opens a fire panel the building does not know about. Ask them, on that call, for the site asbestos register and asbestos management plan and for any arc flash study or fault level labelling on the main switchboard.

Two people on site whenever a panel is opened with 240 V present, a battery bank is handled, or a switchboard is worked on. No solo energised work, ever. A second pair of hands is NOT a safety observer — for energised work the second person must meet the safety observer definition set out in the 'When this SWMS is required' section of this statement.

Confirm you hold the right ticket for what is planned — electrical work licence for the 240 V side, QBCC fire protection licence for the fire system side — AND that you are on Safe QLD's list of workers authorised to perform energised electrical work. You do not self-certify: the business authorises the work, after consulting the person with management or control of the workplace (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 199(1)(e)).

Fatigue. Energised work, switchboard work and battery work is not started at the end of a full day's work. An after-hours impairment is planned as its own shift, with its own start time and its own crew. If the crew has been on shift longer than the maximum in Safe QLD's fatigue policy, or has not had the minimum break that policy requires, the energised work does not start — the system goes back in service, or the fire watch stands up, and the work resumes on a fresh shift.

Leads, tools, test instruments and task lighting inspected and within test tag or calibration date, and looked over before use. A damaged lead comes out of service and gets tagged out — it does not get taped.

MONITORING: the lead technician signs the job card at the start confirming every worker on the job has read and signed on to this SWMS, and that what is actually on site matches the plan. If the site does not match the plan, stop and re-plan before the first cover comes off.

steps.step: Sign in, isolate the system from the brigade and put it out of service
hazards: Building left without automatic fire brigade call while the system is impaired
Unwanted alarm and a brigade attendance charge on the client
Occupants and the warden unaware the system is down
System left isolated overnight because the job ran over
Impairment running past the planned window into a night shift with a tired crew

controls.control: Ring the monitoring provider and isolate the ASE for this job. Write the isolation reference number on the job card before you touch anything.
Make the AS 1851 out-of-service entry in the site log book: time out, exactly what is impaired, your name, expected time back.

Tell the occupier in writing (job note or email) that the installation is impaired and that a fire watch for the impaired area is theirs to provide while it is out — the Building Fire Safety Regulation 2008 (Qld) duty to maintain the prescribed fire safety installation sits with them.
Press the ASE isolate at the FIP and hang the SYSTEM ISOLATED tag on the panel door so the next person through the door can see it.

Cap the impairment at one working day. If you cannot restore it, you do not leave until the occupier has a fire watch physically in place. If restoring it would mean pushing a tired crew into energised work, the fire watch stands up and the work resumes on a fresh shift — see the fatigue control in the planning step.

MONITORING: the ASE isolation reference, the log book entry time and the occupier's written notification are all on the job card before the first cover comes off. The lead technician checks all three.

steps.responsible: Technician, with the building occupier for the fire watch

steps.step: Find the supply, isolate it, lock it, tag it, keep the key on you
hazards: 240 V single phase at the FIP; 400 V three phase at the main switchboard and pump controller
Someone closing the breaker while your hands are in the panel
More than one source of supply — mains, battery bank, UPS, generator changeover, a networked sub-panel
Isolating the wrong circuit because the board schedule is wrong or thirty years old

controls.control: De-energise. That is the job — the hazard is removed, not managed. Energised work happens only where an exception in Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 195(1) genuinely applies, is recorded, and is authorised under s 199(1)(e).

Isolate at the dedicated fire supply circuit breaker at the main switchboard (usually labelled FIRE or FIP, red handle). Apply your own personal lock and a danger tag carrying your name, date and mobile number. The tag is a warning sign attached to the device in a prominent position and suitable in the circumstances, having regard to AS 1319 (Safety signs for the occupational environment) — required by Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 198(2)(a) whenever the device is not under your sole effective control.
Kill every source, not just the obvious one: mains breaker, the panel battery link or fuse, any UPS, and the generator changeover feeding the same board.

Where the breaker will not take a lock, you must still do one of the two things Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 198(2)(b) allows — lock the device in the open position (breaker lock-off device, lockable shroud), or physically prevent it being accidentally closed (rack the breaker off the busbars, remove the circuit cables from the fuse or breaker, pull the fuse carrier and keep it in your pocket, or insert a mechanical restriction). A tag on its own is not an isolation.
One lock per person on the hasp. Nobody removes another person's lock. Last worker off the job is the last lock off.
Before you throw it, check the board schedule and ask the building manager what else is fed from it. Warn them, then switch.

MONITORING: the second worker independently confirms the lock and tag are on the right device, at the right board, before the first cover comes off, and initials the job card. Two sets of eyes on the isolation, every time.

steps.step: Prove dead — test before touch, every time, on every conductor
hazards: Conductors assumed dead that are still live from a second supply or a borrowed neutral
A faulty or flat voltage indicator reading dead on a live circuit
Backfeed onto a submain from the far end
Stored charge in the charger and in filter capacitors after isolation
Conductors proved dead at the point of work while the mains block, transformer and charger a hand's width away are still live

controls.control: Where a cable could be fed from the far end, prove dead at both ends and lock both ends before you cut. Treat every exposed part as energised until it is isolated and found not to be energised (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 196(2)(a)).
Two-pole voltage indicator suited to the work, CAT III or CAT IV rated for the point of use, in test date, with a proving unit. A non-contact pen is never the proof.

Prove, test, prove. Prove the indicator on a known live source or the proving unit, test the conductors, then prove the indicator again. If it fails the second prove, the test never happened — start again with a different instrument.
Test the lot: active-neutral, active-earth, neutral-earth, and phase-to-phase on a three-phase submain. Test at the point of work, not back at the board.
Give the charger and any filter capacitors time to discharge, then prove the DC side dead as well as the AC side before you touch it. An isolated charger is not a discharged charger.

Insulating gloves and face shield stay on until the conductors at the point of work are proved dead AND every remaining live part inside the enclosure is shrouded or barriered. Inside an FIP the mains block, transformer and charger stay live behind the door even when the field wiring is dead — the gloves stay on until those are covered, not until the meter reads zero.

steps.step: Open the fire indicator panel and work inside it
hazards: 240 V mains terminal block, transformer primary and charger board live behind the door even when the field wiring is dead
Dropped screwdriver, torch or rule shorting across the terminal rail — arc flash in an enclosed cabinet at face height
ELV detection loops still fed from a networked panel or sub-panel elsewhere in the building, often in another tenancy
Sharp door edges, unsupported hinged chassis, cabinet at eye level
Anyone standing within 3 m of the exposed mains block, transformer or charger is in energised electrical work — not just the person with hands in the panel
Arc-rated PPE chosen by feel because nobody established the incident energy at this panel

controls.control: Do the work with the FIP mains isolated at the board and proved dead. That removes the 240 V hazard inside the cabinet instead of managing it. Everything below is for the parts that cannot be made dead.
The door interlock, the key switch and the panel ON/OFF are not isolations. The only isolation is the breaker at the board, locked and tagged as set out in the isolation step.
Shroud or barrier the mains terminal block, transformer and charger before any hand or tool goes past them. Insulating mat — rated, in test date and dry — over what you cannot remove.

On a networked system, establish the network topology from the as-builts before you open anything. Identify every panel that can feed the segment you are working on, isolate each one, apply a lock at each one, and prove the loop dead at the point of work. The loop can be fed from a panel three floors away.
1000 V insulated hand tools to AS IEC 60900 (Live working — Hand tools for use up to 1000 V a.c. and 1500 V d.c.), in test date and looked over for nicks and splits before use.
Metal torch, steel rule, watch, rings, neck chain and lanyard off and in the toolbox before the door opens.
Work with your body out of the panel plane, one hand where you can, feet on the insulating mat. Do not lean into a cabinet.

Where a feeding panel is in another tenancy, another building, or under another party's control, name the person who controls access to it, get their agreement in writing before you isolate, and confirm nobody will restore it while you are in the panel. If you cannot secure it, treat the loop as live and work to the energised testing step.

'Near' has a legal meaning: within 3 m of an exposed energised part (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 193). Once the door is open with the mains block, transformer or charger exposed, everyone inside that 3 m is in energised electrical work. Only persons authorised by Safe QLD are in that area (s 201), and everyone in it is kept from inadvertently contacting an exposed energised part (s 202).

Establish the incident energy before you pick your PPE: read the panel or switchboard arc flash label or the site's arc flash study if there is one; if there is not, get the prospective fault current and the protective device clearing time for the board feeding this panel from the drawings, the board schedule or the supply authority, and select arc-rated PPE to suit. If the energy cannot be established, treat it as high energy and do not open it live.

Before you reach in: check the hinged chassis or gear plate is on its stay or is supported, and that the door is held open and cannot swing back on you. Cabinets at eye level cut hands and heads on sheet metal edges — deburred edge protection or gaffer tape on any sharp edge you have to work past, and gloves on.

Arc-rated long sleeves and trousers to the ATPV Safe QLD's PPE schedule sets for panel work (or the incident energy determined above, whichever is higher), safety glasses, and Class 0 insulating gloves with leather overgloves for anything within arm's reach of an exposed live part.

steps.responsible: Licensed electrical worker with a safety observer where any part inside the cabinet is energised

steps.step: Energised testing where the work genuinely cannot be done dead
hazards: Electric shock and electrocution from contact with an exposed live part
Arc flash and arc blast from a slipped probe or a shorted test lead
A live open panel left unattended in a public plant room
No help within reach if the worker goes down
Work started on habit rather than on a recorded exception — no risk assessment, no authorisation, no observer
A second worker or a passing contractor stepping inside 3 m without rated PPE

controls.control: Do it dead. Fault finding and commissioning very often can be. If the work can be done with the equipment de-energised, it must be — none of the four exceptions in Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 195(1) is available to you, and performing the work energised without one is an offence.

Only persons authorised by Safe QLD enter the immediate area while the work is performed (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 201). Rope, tape or barrier the approach and post the observer at it. Nobody inside the arc flash boundary who is not required for the work, and nobody inside it without the rated PPE.

Everyone — you, the observer, anyone walking past — is prevented from inadvertently making contact with an exposed energised part (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 202). Barrier or shroud every live part you are not actually working on, and work on one conductor at a time.
Insulated probes with finger guards, and fused test leads rated for the point of use. Barriers over adjacent live parts.

Before the work starts, a competent person conducts a risk assessment for this specific job and RECORDS the result (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 199(1)(a)). The record goes on the job card and is kept — see the record keeping control below.

A safe work method statement for the proposed energised work is prepared and complies with Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 200 (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 199(1)(b)) — this statement, with the site-specific questions answered and every worker signed on.

The area where the work is to be performed is cleared of obstructions so you can get in and out easily (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 199(1)(c)). Ladders, toolboxes, spares, cable drums and rubbish moved out of the way before the cover comes off.

The point at which the equipment can be disconnected or isolated from supply is clearly marked or labelled, clear of obstructions so you or another competent person can reach it easily, and capable of being operated quickly (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 199(1)(d)). Walk the observer to that point and have them confirm all three before the work starts — under pressure, that is the breaker they will be reaching for.

Energised electrical work authorisation recorded before work starts, naming WHICH exception in Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 195(1) is relied on — (a) it is necessary in the interests of health and safety that the work is performed on or near the equipment while it is energised, (b) it is necessary that the equipment is energised in order for the work to be performed properly, (c) it is necessary for testing the equipment under s 196(1), or (d) there is no reasonable alternative way of carrying out the work — and stating why. The authorisation is given by the Safe QLD supervisor after consulting the building manager or occupier as the person with management or control of the workplace (s 199(1)(e)). Not the internal supervisor alone.

The work is performed by a competent person whose tools, testing equipment and PPE are suitable for the work, have been properly tested, and are in good working order — and are used properly (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 203(1)(a), s 203(2)). Anything out of test date does not go in the panel.
The work is performed in accordance with this SWMS (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 203(1)(b)). If it cannot be, the work stops.

A safety observer observes the work and does nothing else — no handing tools, no paperwork, no phone. The observer must meet the safety observer definition set out in the 'When this SWMS is required' section. The ONLY case where an observer is not required is where the work consists only of testing AND the recorded s 199(1)(a) risk assessment shows there is no serious risk (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 203(3)). A second pair of hands is not a safety observer.

Rescue gear at the panel before the work starts, laid out where the observer can reach it: insulated rescue hook or a dry, clean length of timber or broom handle carried on the vehicle for the purpose; first aid kit; the vehicle AED; and a phone with signal confirmed standing at that spot in the building.
Never walk away from a live open panel. Door shut and locked if you step out, even for a minute.

RECORD KEEPING: keep the risk assessment for at least 28 days after the work is completed, and this SWMS until the work is completed; keep both for at least 2 years if a serious electrical incident or dangerous electrical event occurs in connection with the work (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 204). A copy stays readily accessible to every worker on the job and available for inspection.

STOP WORK: the residual risk on this step is HIGH and stays HIGH. That is not a licence to proceed on your own authority. If any control in this step cannot be applied exactly as written, the work stops immediately, or as soon as it is safe to do so, and resumes only in accordance with this statement (Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 300(2)). It goes back to the supervisor. If the residual cannot be brought below high, the work is not done energised. Any worker may stop this job at any time, without consequence.

Arc-rated shirt and trousers to the ATPV determined for that board, arc-rated face shield and balaclava, Class 0 (1000 V) insulating gloves with leather overgloves, and safety glasses under the shield.

steps.responsible: Licensed electrical worker, safety observer, and the Safe QLD supervisor giving the authorisation

steps.step: Replace the battery bank
hazards: Arc flash and molten metal from a spanner bridging the terminals — a 24 V bank will deliver hundreds of amps into a dead short
A ring, watch band or metal pen across a terminal welding itself to the skin
Electrolyte burns to skin and eyes
20 to 30 kg lift out of a low cabinet, often at floor level in a cramped riser
Vented (flooded) cells present — hydrogen build-up and free electrolyte. Vented cells are OUT OF SCOPE of this SWMS
A mismatched or undersized replacement bank that will not carry the standby and alarm load in a real fire

controls.control: Identify the cell type before you touch anything. If the bank is vented (flooded) cells, or it sits in a dedicated battery room, STOP. That is work in an area that may have a flammable atmosphere — separate high risk construction work under Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 291(l) — and it needs the flammable atmosphere SWMS with gas testing, ventilation proving and ignition source control. Not this one. Do not open it, do not disconnect it, do not switch anything in that room.

Where the panel manufacturer and AS 1670.1 permit it, fit sealed VRLA cells in place of vented cells. That removes the hydrogen accumulation and the free electrolyte at the source instead of managing them.
Battery link or fuse out first. Disconnect negative before positive; on reassembly, positive on first and negative on last. Never allow a tool to span two terminals.

Insulated spanner, shifter or socket to AS IEC 60900, in test date and looked over before use. Insulating cover over the terminals you are not working on. If a rated tool for the terminal size is not on the vehicle, the battery work does not start.
Rings, watch, chain and metal pens off and out of the panel before the first nut is loosened. This one control removes most battery burns.
Match the replacement to the panel manufacturer's rating and to the standby and alarm capacity AS 1670.1 requires for this system. Do not drop in a mismatched pair to make the fault light go out.

Install and ventilate the bank as the panel manufacturer's installation instructions and AS 1670.1 require for that cabinet. AS 3011 and AS 2676 set voltage and capacity thresholds in their own scope clauses and are aimed at battery rooms and larger installations — a typical FIP standby bank may sit outside them. Check the string voltage and capacity against the scope of the edition you actually hold before you cite either one on a job.
Two-person lift or a battery carry strap for anything over 20 kg. Slide it onto a shelf rather than lifting it clear of a low cabinet.
Date-stamp the new batteries, record the capacity/discharge test result in the log book, and take the old ones off site for recycling — not into the client's bin.
Face shield, chemical (nitrile) gloves and safety glasses on for every battery handled, sealed or not. Eyewash or clean running water confirmed within reach before the first nut is loosened.

steps.step: Cable work — run, terminate and make good to the Wiring Rules
hazards: Cutting into a live cable that was never identified
Drilling into concealed services, or through the far side of a wall into an occupied room
Drilling, cutting or removing material containing asbestos — panel and switchboard backing boards, fibro walls, ceilings and eaves, and old penetration fill and fire-stopping
Fire-rated cable damaged, unsupported, or fixed to services that will fail early in a fire
Segregation lost between ELV fire wiring and 240 V, causing induced faults and unwanted alarms
Fire wall or floor rating destroyed by an unsealed penetration

controls.control: Consult the site asbestos register and the asbestos management plan BEFORE any drilling, cutting, sanding or fixing. The person with management or control of the workplace must have one for a building of this age. No register on site is a stop — you do not put a drill in a wall on the strength of somebody's opinion.
De-energise and lock off the circuit at its source before any cable is cut. Where the cable can be fed from the far end, lock and prove dead at both ends.
Where the drill zone cannot be proved clear of services, de-energise and lock off the circuits serving that wall or floor before drilling, or change the route.

Where a route cannot avoid material that is or is presumed to be asbestos, reroute — surface mount, use an existing penetration, or come in from a clear substrate. Rerouting is cheaper than an asbestos job every time.
Fire-rated cable where AS 1670.1 calls for it, supported and fixed so the rating survives the fire — never cable-tied to sprinkler pipe, conduit, ceiling grid or another service.
Keep the segregation the Wiring Rules (AS/NZS 3000) require between ELV fire wiring and low voltage wiring: separate enclosure, or a barriered section of the same enclosure.
Reinstate every penetration with a tested and approved fire-stopping system matched to the rating of the wall or floor you went through. Photograph it before it is covered.

If the material is asbestos, or is unknown and of an age or appearance to be presumed asbestos-containing, STOP. Do not drill, cut, sand, scrape or break it. Disturbance of asbestos is separate high risk construction work under Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 291(d): it needs its own SWMS, and licensed removal where the work is licensed asbestos removal work. Ring the office before you do anything else.

Positively identify the cable at both ends and prove dead at the point of cut. If you cannot positively identify it, you do not cut it — go back and find the other end. Tracing and proving is a human check, not a barrier: it is only as good as the person doing it.

Cable detector over the wall, check the drawings, and look at the far side before drilling. Treat a clear scan as an aid, not proof — detectors miss deep runs, shielded and de-energised cable, and anything inside steel conduit.
Size conductors and protection with the actual route length and voltage drop calculated by the AS/NZS 3008.1.1 method — not eyeballed off the last job.
MONITORING: fire-stopping, cable support and segregation are checked and photographed by a second person before anything is covered or a ceiling goes back, and the photos go on the job.

steps.step: Work on the submain feeding the fire pump
hazards: Hydrant and sprinkler systems left with no pump — the building has no firefighting water while you are on the submain
High fault energy at the main switchboard: arc flash burns far worse than anything at a FIP
The pumpset starting on you mid-job from the pressure line, the jockey pump, or an auto-start signal
Back-feed from the pump controller or a second supply
The busbar and the supply side of the fire pump breaker stay live and cannot be isolated at the board — the breaker can be dead on the load side while its own terminals are live behind it
Protection or supply arrangement altered in a way that will drop the pump out in a real fire
Arc-rated PPE picked by habit at the highest energy board on the site because nobody established the incident energy

controls.control: Isolate and lock the submain at both ends: the fire pump circuit breaker at the main switchboard and the isolator at the pumpset controller. Prove dead at both ends, at the point of work.

Isolate the pumpset controller and the jockey pump, and shut and lock the start pressure line where the design allows, so the pump cannot start while you are on it. Record every isolation you make — you have to undo all of them at handback.

Barrier or shroud the busbar chamber and the supply side of the fire pump breaker before any tool goes in. Physically mark what is not to be touched and brief the observer on it by pointing at it, not by describing it.

Keep the supply as AS 2941 requires: dedicated, protected and labelled for the pumpset. Do not add an RCD, do not share the submain with other loads, and do not fit protection that will trip on locked rotor or during a real fire run.

Where the work goes to the supply side of the main switch, it is planned in the office as energised work under Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) ss 195 and 199 — note that s 199(2)(a) relaxes only the 'clear of obstructions' precondition for that work, not the risk assessment, the SWMS, the isolation point requirement or the authorisation — OR the main switch is dropped, OR the supply authority is engaged to pull the service fuses. It is not decided at the board on the day.

Establish the incident energy before you select PPE: read the site's arc flash study or the switchboard label if there is one; if there is not, get the prospective fault current and the protective device clearing time for that board from the drawings, the switchboard schedule or the supply authority, and select arc-rated PPE to suit. If the energy cannot be established, treat the board as high energy and do not open it live.

Reinstate or replace the FIRE PUMP — DO NOT SWITCH OFF labelling at the main switchboard and at the controller before you leave the room. Signage is the last thing that stops the next person, and it is the first thing that gets left off.
Record the pumpset impairment in the log book and tell the occupier in writing that hydrants and sprinklers have no pump for the duration. Fire watch for the whole impairment, not part of it.

Arc-rated shirt and trousers to the ATPV determined for that board (higher than the FIP figure — dress for the board you are standing at, not the one you were at this morning), arc-rated face shield and balaclava, Class 0 insulating gloves with leather overgloves, safety glasses and hearing protection.

steps.responsible: Licensed electrical worker with safety observer

steps.step: Test and verify the installation before you energise it
hazards: Energising onto a fault — arc flash at the board
Missing or high-resistance earth leaving the panel enclosure live under fault
Reversed polarity at a terminal or an outlet
Loop cards and detector electronics destroyed by a 500 V insulation test
Results written up later from memory and not matching what the instrument actually read

controls.control: The installation stays isolated, locked and tagged for the whole of the verification. Locks come off only after every test is complete and every reading is written down.

Run the verification the Wiring Rules (AS/NZS 3000) require before the installation is energised: visual inspection, continuity of the earthing system, insulation resistance, polarity, correct circuit connections, and RCD operation where fitted. Use the inspection and test methods in AS/NZS 3017 — confirm the current edition of both before you rely on a clause number.
Disconnect the panel electronics, loop cards and any surge device before insulation testing. 500 V into a loop card is a return visit and a new board.
Instruments in calibration/test date and function-checked on a known reference before use.
Write the actual readings on the test sheet at the time, at the board. Not from memory in the ute afterwards.

Certificate of Testing and Compliance: the licensed electrical CONTRACTOR who connects the installation to a source of electricity must, as soon as practicable after the connection, give the person for whom the work was performed a certificate stating that person's name and address, the electrical installation tested, the day it was tested, and the identifying number of the electrical contractor licence under which it was tested, and certifying that the installation, to the extent it is affected by the work, has been tested to ensure it is electrically safe and complies with the requirements of the wiring rules (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 229(2)-(4)). The contractor keeps a copy for at least 5 years (s 229(5)). Attach a copy to the job. This duty is the contractor's, not the individual technician's — make sure the office knows the connection was made.

steps.responsible: Licensed electrical worker; the licensed electrical contractor for the Certificate of Testing and Compliance

steps.step: Re-energise, restore the fire system and the pumpset, and hand it back
hazards: Closing the breaker while someone still has hands in the panel
System left isolated from the brigade after everyone goes home
A fault or disablement left standing on the panel and nobody told
A zone, loop or device that was disturbed left dead while one test detector passes and the panel shows normal
Pumpset left isolated, or the start pressure line left shut — the panel shows normal and the building has no firefighting water
Client believing the system is protecting them when it is not

controls.control: Nobody's hands go near the panel while the breaker is being closed. The panel is closed up and the cover is on before the mains is restored, and locks stay on until the head count is done.
Head count and a shout down the riser before the breaker is closed. Your lock is the last one off, and only you take it off.
Restore in reverse order: panel closed up, mains on, battery link in, charging confirmed, all disablements removed, panel showing normal.

Restore the pumpset under control: confirm nobody is at the pumpset or in the pump room, restore the start pressure line, remove the controller and jockey pump isolations and locks, re-energise, verify auto-start operates and the controller shows normal with no alarms, confirm the FIRE PUMP — DO NOT SWITCH OFF labelling is back at both ends, and record it in the AS 1851 log. The pump is proved running, not assumed available.

Test every device, zone and circuit that was disturbed — not a sample — plus one detector and one call point end-to-end through to the brigade. Ring the monitoring provider, de-isolate the ASE, confirm with them that the signal was received, and record the reference.
Verify battery charging voltage and current, and confirm the standby and alarm capacity result recorded at the battery step against what AS 1670.1 requires for this system.

Confirm ALL outputs, not just the brigade path — ASE, occupant warning and EWIS, and any fan, lift, door-hold, damper or shutter interface. Confirm the panel is clear of faults and disablements before you write anything down.

Close out the AS 1851 log book: time back in service, and a list of what was actually tested — the words 'system normal' on their own are not a record. Photograph the panel showing a clear, normal condition.
Tell the occupier and the chief warden face to face or by phone that the system is back in service, what was done, and that the fire watch can stand down. Do not leave that to an email nobody reads.

MONITORING AND REVIEW: before you leave, close this SWMS out. Every worker signed on; the site-specific questions answered; the recorded risk assessment and this statement returned to the office with the job and filed against it. Anything that did not work as written — a control you could not apply, a hazard nobody had listed, a near miss — is raised as a SWMS review item that day, not at the next toolbox.

steps.responsible: Technician and building occupier; lead technician for the SWMS close-out

emergency:
BEFORE ANY ENERGISED WORK STARTS — the safety observer is shown the isolation point and confirms out loud that it is clearly marked or labelled, clear of obstructions, and capable of being operated quickly (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 199(1)(d)). Under pressure that is the breaker they will be reaching for, and there is no time to look for it.

ELECTRIC SHOCK — do not grab the person. Kill the supply at the breaker you locked and confirmed, or drag them clear with a dry insulated rescue hook, dry timber or dry rope. Then call 000, start CPR and use the defibrillator — the one carried on the vehicle for energised work, plus the building's own if it has one. Every shock victim goes to hospital even if they say they are fine: a low voltage shock can cause a delayed cardiac event hours later. This is a notifiable event. A serious electrical incident or a dangerous electrical event under the Electrical Safety Act 2002 (Qld) must be notified to the Electrical Safety Office / Workplace Health and Safety Queensland on 1300 362 128 — ring the Safe QLD supervisor immediately and make sure the notification is actually made, using those words. Do not disturb the site: nothing at the panel or board is moved, repaired or made good until an inspector arrives or directs otherwise — except so far as is necessary to help an injured person, to remove a further risk to health or safety, or as a police officer or inspector directs. Keep the recorded risk assessment and this SWMS for at least 2 years after a serious electrical incident or dangerous electrical event (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 204(3)).

ARC FLASH OR BURNS — cool with cool running water for 20 minutes. Do not peel clothing off a burn and do not apply creams or ice. Call 000 for any burn to the face, hands or airway, or larger than a palm.

BATTERY ACID — flush skin or eyes with the eyewash or clean running water for at least 15 minutes and keep flushing on the way to hospital. Remove contaminated clothing while flushing.

FIRE IN THE PANEL OR SWITCHBOARD — isolate only if you can safely reach the breaker. CO2 extinguisher, never water on live gear. If it does not go out immediately, get out and shut the door.

FIRE ANYWHERE IN THE BUILDING WHILE THE SYSTEM IS ISOLATED — the brigade will not be called automatically. Call 000 yourself, give the street address, and tell them the fire system is out of service and which areas are affected. Then ring the monitoring provider and the chief warden.

PERSON TRAPPED OR UNCONSCIOUS IN A PLANT ROOM OR PIT — do not enter. Call 000 and wait. More rescuers die than victims.

SUSPECTED ASBESTOS DISTURBED — stop, leave the drill or saw where it is, get everyone out of the area and keep them out, do not sweep or vacuum, and ring the office. The area stays closed until it has been assessed.

EVERY INCIDENT — photographs, log book entry, and a report to the office the same day, before you go home. Any control in this SWMS that did not work, or could not be applied, is raised as a review item the same day.

siteSpecificPrompts: Where is the fire indicator panel mains supply isolated — which switchboard, which breaker, what circuit number, and is it labelled correctly?
Can that breaker physically take a lock, or do you need a lock-off device, to rack it off the busbars, or to pull the fuse carrier?
Is the isolation point clearly marked, clear of obstructions, reachable and quick to operate — and has the safety observer been walked to it and confirmed it?
Is there a second supply into the panel — UPS, generator changeover, a networked sub-panel, or a shared neutral with another circuit?
On a networked system: which panels can feed the segment you are working on, where are they, who controls access to each, and do you have their written agreement not to restore them?
Where is the fire pump submain isolated at the switchboard end and at the controller end, and can both be locked?

Does any part of this job go to the supply side of the main switch? If so, who has planned it, and how — energised work under ss 195 and 199, main switch dropped, or supply authority to pull the service fuses?
What else drops out when you isolate that board, and who needs to be warned first?
Is there an arc flash study or fault level labelling on the main switchboard? If not, what is the prospective fault current and clearing time for that board, and what ATPV does that call for?
Is there a site asbestos register and asbestos management plan? Have you seen it? What does it say about the panel backing board, the wall you are drilling, and the existing penetrations?
Who is the site contact and chief warden today, and what is their mobile number?
Which monitoring company holds the ASE, and what is the account or reference number needed to isolate it?
Is the battery bank sealed VRLA or vented (flooded)? If vented, stop — this SWMS does not cover it. What is the string voltage, capacity and cell weight?
Is the pump room, tank or valve pit a confined space, or does it have a below-ground pit?
Do you have mobile signal standing at the panel? If not, who is the standby person and where do you go to call 000?
Where is the nearest first aid kit, defibrillator (yours on the vehicle and the building's), eyewash and CO2 extinguisher, and where is the muster point?
Can the system be impaired during business hours, or does this need to be an after-hours job with the occupier's agreement — and if after hours, is it planned as its own shift with a fresh crew?
How long has the crew been on shift, and does the fatigue policy allow this energised work to start?
Who is providing the fire watch for the duration of the impairment, and have they been told in writing?
Which version of this SWMS is on the job, has every worker signed on to it, and does the principal contractor have a copy where one is required?
